glossaryEntries.definition: The word obeyed to completeness — “My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, and to finish his work”; and the will is the word: where Matthew hears “do the will of my Father,” Luke records the same saying as “hear the word of God, and do it.” Milk and meat are one substance in two states — the word received, and the word done: chewed and tasted as the ear tries words, served in due season, its fruit senses exercised to discern.
glossaryEntries.citations: (John 4:34; 6:55; 7:17; Matt 12:50; Luke 8:21; Ps 40:8; Job 34:3; Heb 5:14; Matt 24:45) · see Introduction, ch. 1

glossaryEntries.definition: Covenant loyalty — the Hebrew is chesed, the word beneath most of the Bible's “mercy”: the debt canceled for the one who “confesseth and forsaketh,” kept “with them that love him and keep his commandments,” and required of the pardoned — “blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.”
glossaryEntries.commonView: Commonly taught: not getting the punishment you do deserve — a one-way transaction, no conditions named.
glossaryEntries.citations: (Deut 7:9; Prov 28:13; Matt 18:27-35; 5:7) · see Grace, Mercy & the Gift, ch. 24

glossaryEntries.definition: The word received — teaching another has already digested, swallowed without work; the right first food of babes, given to grow them, and meant to be outgrown at weaning. Churned, it becomes butter — the word worked toward solid food.
glossaryEntries.citations: (1 Pet 2:2; 1 Cor 3:1-2; Isa 28:9; 7:15; Prov 30:33; Heb 5:12-13) · see Introduction, ch. 1

glossaryEntries.definition: The instant of decisive action, built on the image of an eye's wink — the unit in which judgment and mercy alike are done, never a slow process: Babylon falls “in a moment… in one day,” and the dead are raised “in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye.”
glossaryEntries.citations: (Isa 47:9; Job 34:20; 1 Cor 15:52) · see The Moment, ch. 38 | (Isa 47:9; Job 34:20; 1 Cor 15:52) · see The Moment, in the free digital edition at TimeTested.Bible

glossaryEntries.definition: The faithful witness — the Son, who shines with no light of His own but the Father's reflected, the light that shineth in the world's night; the lesser light that rules the night and marks the appointed times.
glossaryEntries.commonView: Commonly taught: the church reflecting Christ's light as the moon reflects the sun.
glossaryEntries.citations: (Ps 89:37; Rev 1:5; John 1:5; 5:19) · see Sun, Moon & Stars, ch. 29

glossaryEntries.definition: A kingdom — the seat of ruling authority.
glossaryEntries.citations: (Jer 51:25; Dan 2:35) · see Mountain, ch. 39

glossaryEntries.definition: Without covenant covering — exposed in one's breach.
glossaryEntries.citations: (Ezek 16:8; Gen 3:7) · see Garments & Armor, ch. 43

glossaryEntries.definition: The covenant identity of a house, consisting of 3 things appointed and provided by its Head: the Word (the manna), the covenant law (the stone tables), and the fruitful priesthood (Aaron's budded rod). A counterfeit Name substitutes a different word, covenant, or priesthood; a Name is taken in vain when any one is rejected, replaced, or removed. A bride takes her Husband's Name by entering His house, coming under His authority, and obeying Him.
glossaryEntries.commonView: Commonly taught: the person's character, authority, and reputation.

glossaryEntries.definition: The gospel’s gathering of all kinds out of the sea of peoples.
glossaryEntries.citations: (Matt 13:47-48) · see Sea & Waters, ch. 40

glossaryEntries.definition: The renewed moon — chodesh, from chadash, to renew: the phase of the moon that serves as the sign of the start of the month, and so the name of the month itself. A sign must be watched for: the east gate opens on it for worship, commerce resents it, and Paul files it among the shadows of things to come; which phase renews the month, the Pearl chapter weighs from the letters.
glossaryEntries.citations: (Ps 81:3; 1 Sam 20:5, 18; Isa 66:23; Ezek 46:1-3; Amos 8:5; Col 2:16-17) · see The Pearls of Wisdom, ch. 31

glossaryEntries.definition: A newly conferred covenant identity under its giver — known, received, and kept only by the one who bears it.
glossaryEntries.commonView: Commonly taught: a new God-given identity and character bestowed on the overcomer.
glossaryEntries.citations: (Gen 32:28; Isa 62:2-5; 65:15; Rev 2:17) · see Love, Knowing, Faith & Belief, ch. 6

glossaryEntries.definition: The time of darkness — hiding and sleep, when opportunity closes; the children of the night sleep and are drunken, doing their deeds in the dark.
glossaryEntries.citations: (Gen 1:5; 1 Thess 5:5-7) · see Light and Darkness, ch. 21

glossaryEntries.definition: A great city of the sea — gentile peoples who repent and rise in judgment.
glossaryEntries.citations: (Matt 12:41) · see The Sign of Jonah, ch. 4

glossaryEntries.definition: The hidden quarter — tsaphon, from the root to hide, to lurk: the dark side of the sky, the door the ambush comes by. In the north country the spoilers of Babylon gather — “an assembly of great nations,” the ten allied kings who turn on the seven the whore rules — and in its uttermost recesses, the “sides of the north,” the enemy set his seat.
glossaryEntries.citations: (Jer 1:14; 50:9, 41; 51:48; Ps 48:2; Isa 14:13; Rev 17:16-18) · see The Fall of Babylon, ch. 35, and Lucifer's Declared Plan, ch. 30

glossaryEntries.definition: The commandment's truth and correction received and laid up inwardly until they govern the life — the tested, pressed fruit of the Spirit stored as proven obedience; light is that obedience made visible as an example to others.
glossaryEntries.commonView: Commonly taught: the Holy Spirit — anointing, consecration, and empowering.

glossaryEntries.definition: Israel, the covenant people.
glossaryEntries.citations: (Jer 11:16; Hos 9:10) · see Trees, ch. 41

glossaryEntries.definition: The covenant made whole — shalom, from a root meaning to complete, restore, repay: the work of righteousness, the great peace of them that love the law — not the world’s truce and not a feeling (“not as the world giveth”). What the gospel publishes is this peace restored; the counterfeit pronounces it twice over an unkept covenant — “Peace, peace; when there is no peace.”

The one complete light — under the KJV's “rubies” (peninim, Strong's pearl), wisdom and the bride are priced above pearls; and the night sky's one pearl is the full moon (keseh, “fulness,” the letters under “throne” and “time appointed”), governor of the appointed times, the one-pearl gates of the city — the merchant's entry at the King's gate.
glossaryEntries.commonView: Commonly taught: the kingdom of heaven, worth surrendering everything to gain — or the church, purchased by Christ.
glossaryEntries.citations: (Prov 3:15; 31:10; Ps 81:3; Prov 7:20; Job 26:9; Ps 104:19; Rev 21:21) · see The Pearls of Wisdom, ch. 31

glossaryEntries.definition: The bowed-humble before God — one Hebrew word family behind “poor” and “meek,” and “needy” (evyon) its constant companion; empty-handed toward Him, and so able to receive: the gospel’s hearers and heirs of the kingdom.
glossaryEntries.citations: (Ps 37:11/Matt 5:5; Isa 61:1/Luke 4:18; Isa 66:2; Jas 2:5; Ps 72:12-13) · see Orphans, Widows & the Fatherless, ch. 14

glossaryEntries.definition: The faithful few who glean the edge — widow, fatherless, stranger, as Ruth did; small by design, refined like gold out of dross, at a fixed ratio traceable from the gleaning law's own geometry to Elijah's seven thousand.
glossaryEntries.citations: (Ruth 2; 1 Kgs 19:18; Zech 13:8-9; Rom 11:5) · see The Remnant, ch. 15

glossaryEntries.definition: The self-sufficient who “have need of nothing” — full of self, and so unable to receive; Laodicea's boast, and Smyrna's opposite. The true wealth is being “rich toward God”: faith tried in the fire, and the garment of righteousness.
glossaryEntries.citations: (Rev 3:17-18; Rev 2:9; Prov 13:7; Luke 12:21) · see Orphans, Widows & the Fatherless, ch. 14

glossaryEntries.definition: Right-living. God is Right-Living by definition — His ways and works are the measure of right. For those under His authority, right-living is the doing of His commandments: the law kept, worn as the garment of righteous acts. Romans 4 excludes wage-work that would put God in debt, not obedience; even complete obedience earns no wage because the servant has only done his duty. Righteousness is given and reckoned by grace, but the gift never renames wrong-living right.
glossaryEntries.commonView: Commonly taught: primarily right standing before God — Christ's imputed righteousness received by faith apart from works — with right-living as its subsequent fruit and evidence.
glossaryEntries.citations: (Deut 32:4; 6:25; Ps 119:172; 145:17; Luke 17:7-10; Rom 4:4-8; Phil 3:9; Heb 11:8; 1 John 3:7) · see Love, Knowing, Faith & Belief, ch. 6, for the dependent definitions; The End of the Law for Paul's wage, debt, law, and obedience vocabulary; and Garments & Armor, ch. 43, for righteousness given and worn

glossaryEntries.definition: The covenant — the Rock that followed Israel “was Christ,” the covenant in person; the stone the builders refused, made the cornerstone.
glossaryEntries.citations: (Deut 32:4; Isa 42:6; 1 Cor 10:4; Ps 118:22) · see Mountain, ch. 39

glossaryEntries.definition: The complete seven — six-and-one as a single whole, at every scale the law counts it: the week whose seventh day is the rest, the seventh year that rests the land, the seven-sevens that ring in jubilee. Scripture counts “seven sabbaths complete” and calls the week itself the sabbath; the rest-day is the crown of the unit, one-seventh of what the word names.
glossaryEntries.citations: (Lev 23:15 with Deut 16:9; Lev 25:2-8; 2 Chr 36:21; Luke 18:12; Matt 28:1; Heb 4:9) · see The Sabbath, ch. 32 | (Lev 23:15 with Deut 16:9; Lev 25:2-8; 2 Chr 36:21; Luke 18:12; Matt 28:1; Heb 4:9) · see The Sabbath, in the free digital edition at TimeTested.Bible

glossaryEntries.definition: To cause, appoint, or acknowledge as holy — removing someone or something from common status, placing it under an owner's claim for an appointed purpose, and treating or preparing it accordingly. God sanctifies by claiming for Himself and fitting for His use; people sanctify God and His Name by treating and displaying Him as holy. Moral cleansing and obedient living fit a person to that holy calling, but they are not the word's entire meaning.
glossaryEntries.commonView: Commonly taught: God's progressive work of inward renewal, by which believers die more and more to sin and live in righteousness.
glossaryEntries.citations: (Ex 13:2; Num 8:17; Isa 8:13; Ezek 36:23; John 10:36; 17:19; 1 Cor 7:14; 1 Thess 4:3-7; 2 Tim 2:21; Heb 10:10, 29) · see Uncommon Sanctification, Justification, and Cleanliness

glossaryEntries.definition: The countless multitude — grains of the shore beyond number; and so a shifting foundation: to build on the sand is to build on the crowd, not the covenant-rock.
glossaryEntries.citations: (Gen 22:17; Hos 1:10; Rev 20:8; Matt 7:26) · see Sea & Waters, ch. 40

glossaryEntries.definition: Covenant blood made wearable — and counterfeited by those who wear the form without the substance.
glossaryEntries.citations: (Isa 1:18; Josh 2:18; Heb 9:19; Rev 17:4) · see Garments & Armor, ch. 43 — derived in the digital edition’s symbol study at TimeTested.Bible

glossaryEntries.definition: Peoples and nations — the restless, unrooted mass below the firmament; and, above it, the gathered waters of heaven: the still sea of glass where the angels and the redeemed stand.
glossaryEntries.citations: (Rev 17:15; Gen 1:6-8; Ps 148:4; Rev 4:6; 15:2) · see Sea & Waters, ch. 40

glossaryEntries.definition: The NAME impressed on its owner — the signet-plate the law sets on the priest's forehead (HOLINESS TO THE LORD), the law bound on hand and between the eyes, stamped by the Spirit on God's servants before judgment; the inscription is quoted: the Lord knoweth them that are his — let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity. The counterfeit takes the same two places.
The word of God, sown in the hearts of men.

glossaryEntries.definition: The deceiver; the one who strips the covenant covering.
glossaryEntries.citations: (Gen 3:1) · see Sea & Waters, ch. 40 — derived in the digital edition’s symbol study at TimeTested.Bible

glossaryEntries.definition: The covering of a greater presence — refuge under the Almighty's wings, a kingdom's protection over its people, the outline a coming body casts ahead of itself. Good to dwell in — not the gloom it is read as; the KJV itself renders the word “defence”.
glossaryEntries.citations: (Ps 91:1; Num 14:9; Col 2:17) · see Shadow, ch. 17

glossaryEntries.definition: The covenant people, who hear the Shepherd's voice and follow.
glossaryEntries.citations: (John 10:27) · see Love, Knowing, Faith & Belief, ch. 6

glossaryEntries.definition: The demanding place — from sha'al, to demand: mortality's claim on all flesh, swallowing righteous and wicked alike, personified with a mouth, gates, and bars. Its dead sleep in silence until it is made to give them back; then it is itself destroyed — “O grave, I will be thy destruction.” Distinct from Gehenna, the judgment.
glossaryEntries.citations: (Gen 37:35; Ps 16:10; Eccl 9:5; Isa 5:14; Hos 13:14; Rev 20:13-14) · see Heaven and Hell, ch. 16

glossaryEntries.definition: An earthly kingdom, city, state, or governed political body riding upon the sea of peoples: its rulers guide it, its inhabitants and servants crew it, its armies defend it, and its wealth is carried as cargo. Christ needs no constructed body beneath Him: He walks upon the sea directly, and when He sails with His disciples the vessel comes under its true Head. The ship may be broken while its people survive.
glossaryEntries.commonView: Commonly taught: the Church — a vessel of salvation carrying believers through the dangers of the world.

glossaryEntries.definition: A prophecy given in advance — often a prophet's lived story — whose fulfillment testifies; not a wonder performed on demand.
glossaryEntries.commonView: Commonly taught: a miraculous act pointing to God's power and Christ's identity.
glossaryEntries.citations: (Isa 7:14; Ezek 24:24; Luke 11:30) · see Signs and Similitudes, ch. 3

glossaryEntries.definition: The transgression of the law — Scripture's own definition: “sin is the transgression of the law”; where no law is, there is no transgression, and by the law is the knowledge of sin.
glossaryEntries.citations: (1 John 3:4; Rom 4:15; 3:20; 7:7) · see Grace, Mercy & the Gift, ch. 24

glossaryEntries.definition: A spiritual name of Jerusalem — the prophets address her rulers so to their faces: “Hear the word of the LORD, ye rulers of Sodom… ye people of Gomorrah”; Ezekiel calls Sodom her sister and Jerusalem the worse; and Revelation writes the name on “the great city… where also our Lord was crucified.”
glossaryEntries.citations: (Isa 1:10; Ezek 16:46-48; Rev 11:8) · see The Fall of Babylon, ch. 35

glossaryEntries.definition: The righteous, who rule the night with the Son — “they that be wise shall shine… as the stars for ever”; the twelve stars are the twelve tribes, gathered into the twelve constellations, the Mazzaroth.
glossaryEntries.citations: (Dan 12:3; Ps 136:9; Gen 37:9; Rev 12:1; Job 38:32) · see Sun, Moon & Stars, ch. 29

glossaryEntries.definition: A covenant cut by God — for a covenant is cut (Hebrew karat) — grown into the kingdom that breaks the world-empires and fills the earth.
glossaryEntries.citations: (Dan 2:34-35, 44-45; Gen 15:17-18; Deut 9:10; Col 2:11) · see Mountain, ch. 39

glossaryEntries.definition: The nations in turmoil — the raging sea, stilled at Christ's word, “Peace, be still”.
glossaryEntries.commonView: Commonly taught: divine judgment, and the trials of life which Christ has power to calm.
glossaryEntries.citations: (Ps 65:7; Isa 17:12-13; Mark 4:39; Luke 21:25) · see Sea & Waters, ch. 40

glossaryEntries.definition: A non-citizen of God's commonwealth — one outside the covenant, drawn in, or, once in, made a stranger to the world.
glossaryEntries.citations: (Eph 2:12, 19) · see Orphans, Widows & the Fatherless, ch. 14

glossaryEntries.definition: The Father, the source of light, from which every lesser light is drawn; the righteous shall shine as the sun in His kingdom.
glossaryEntries.citations: (Ps 84:11; Gen 37:9; Matt 13:43) · see Sun, Moon & Stars, ch. 29

glossaryEntries.definition: The unclean beast par excellence — the one beast in the law wearing the outward sign without the inward work: the hoof parted, the cud never chewed. glossaryEntries.citations: (Rev 6:4; Gen 3:24) · see The Four Winds, ch. 34

glossaryEntries.citations: (Isa 9:15-16; Deut 28:13, 44; Rev 12:4; 9:19; Ex 4:4) · see The Fall of Babylon, ch. 35

glossaryEntries.citations: (Matt 13:25-30, 38-40) · see Grass, ch. 42

glossaryEntries.citations: (Isa 40:4) · see Mountain, ch. 39 — derived in the digital edition’s symbol study at TimeTested.Bible

glossaryEntries.definition: One who hears God's word and does it, who fears the LORD.

glossaryEntries.definition: Paul's phrase for deeds considered in relation to law. It is not a synonym for obedience and does not identify one unchanging class of deeds. The surrounding passage may identify God's law, a circumcision-party application, or leave the particular acts unnamed. What remains consistent is the rejected claim made for those deeds: they cannot purchase justification, produce the Spirit, establish covenant standing, or place God in debt. glossaryEntries.definition: To bow down and serve — homage in the body, allegiance in the life; the fear of the LORD made visible, kept at His appointed times, on His terms. Not the song service: Scripture separates worship from singing in single scenes.

glossaryEntries.definition: A turning — shanah, written on the root to change, repeat, return: one complete cycle of time, at whatever scale the count is running — Jeremiah’s seventy “years” close only as seventy jubilees, and a thousand years pass as a day.

entries.definition: To cleanse is to remove the defilement that bars proper contact, approach, or use; clean describes what is free of that defilement and fit for its permitted place. Uncleanness may be physical, ceremonial, or moral and does not always mean guilt: childbirth, marital relations, and touching the dead all make unclean without being called sin. Cleansing removes what makes a vessel unfit; sanctification places the cleansed vessel under a holy claim and appointed use.
entries.commonView: Commonly treated either as hygiene and obsolete ritual regulation, or as a synonym for moral purity and holiness.

judges.label: Claude
judges.consensusMeaning: In mainstream Christian teaching, 'clean/unclean' is understood as ritual-purity language that symbolizes moral and spiritual condition before God: uncleanness represents sin, defilement, and unfitness to approach a holy God, while cleanness represents holiness, moral purity, and acceptable standing in God's presence. Correspondingly, 'cleanse/cleansing' symbolizes God's forgiveness of sin and the sanctification of the believer, accomplished ultimately through the atoning blood of Christ (with the Old Testament washings and purification rites read as types or foreshadowings of that spiritual cleansing). A closely joined sub-theme is Jesus' relocation of defilement from external ritual to the inner heart (Mark 7), and the New Testament's declaration that former ritual categories (foods, Gentiles) are now 'cleansed,' opening covenant access to all peoples.

entries.definition: To judge, declare, or demonstrate a person, word, deed, or cause right against a question or charge; the opposite is to condemn.
